lines.text: Do you know the first flight of an airplane was shorter than the wings of a jumbo jet?
This is the real Wright Flyer, laser scanned by the Smithsonian. Every wire, every rib.
Twelve metres wide. A frame of spruce and ash, covered in cotton muslin.
No car engine was light enough. So their mechanic, Charlie Taylor, built one from scratch. Twelve horsepower.
Bicycle chains drive two hand-carved propellers. One chain is crossed, so they spin in opposite directions.
Their secret was a homemade wind tunnel. In nineteen oh one, they tested two hundred little wings in it.
A curved wing pushes the air down. And the air pushes the wing up. That's lift.
To steer, the pilot swung his hips in a cradle. Wires twisted the wing tips, and turned the rudder.
December seventeenth, nineteen oh three. Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. A strong wind, over thirty kilometres an hour.
The Flyer ran down a wooden rail, straight into the wind. And it lifted off.
Twelve seconds. Thirty-seven metres. A jumbo jet's wings are wider than that.
They flew four times that day. The last flight lasted fifty-nine seconds, and covered two hundred and sixty metres.
Minutes later, a gust of wind flipped the Flyer over. It never flew again.
The Wrights kept their work secret, shared with only a few people. Orbi Transfer Spaces work the same way.
A private Space is a named room with a passcode. Its files never show up in public, and only members can open them.
